feature_request: Add a small sliding-window request counter as a Node.js library with no external dependencies: a Counter class that records a timestamped hit per call to record(), and a count(windowMs) method returning how many hits occurred within the last windowMs milliseconds, pruning older hits as it goes.

output.title: Dependency-free sliding-window request counter
output.description: Provide a package-root CommonJS Node.js library exporting a Counter class that timestamps recorded hits and counts and prunes hits using a caller-supplied sliding window.
requirements: The package root must be consumable as `const Counter = require('.')`, with `module.exports` resolving directly to the class named `Counter` rather than to a wrapper object.
The public constructor interface must be `new Counter()` with no parameters.
Counter must expose `record(): void`; each invocation must capture one timestamp using `Date.now()` and add exactly one hit, including when multiple calls receive the same timestamp.

Counter must expose `count(windowMs: number): number`; it must capture the current time using `Date.now()` and return an integer count of retained hits whose timestamps are within the inclusive interval from `now - windowMs` through `now`.
During each `count(windowMs)` call, every retained hit with a timestamp strictly less than `now - windowMs` must be removed. A hit exactly on the lower boundary must remain and be counted.
Pruning is irreversible: a hit removed by one `count()` call must not reappear in a later count, including a later call using a larger window or an earlier clock value.
Stored hits must be evaluated individually rather than assuming timestamp order, so counting and pruning remain correct when duplicate timestamps occur or `Date.now()` moves backward.
The library and its tests must use only Node.js built-in capabilities and must not add external dependency declarations.
constraints: The exact public arities must be `Counter.length === 0`, `Counter.prototype.record.length === 0`, and `Counter.prototype.count.length === 1`.
For `windowMs === 0`, only retained hits timestamped exactly at the current `Date.now()` value are counted; older hits are pruned and future-dated retained hits are not counted.
Behavior for arguments other than finite, non-negative numeric `windowMs` values is unspecified by this feature request and must not be relied upon by acceptance tests.
Changes must remain limited to the files named in `target_files`.
acceptance_criteria: `require('.')` returns a class named `Counter`, and constructing it with `new Counter()` succeeds with the required constructor and method arities.
A new Counter returns numeric integer `0` from `count(windowMs)` when no hits have been recorded.
Each `record()` call returns `undefined` and contributes exactly one hit to a subsequent count when its timestamp lies inside the requested inclusive window.
Multiple hits recorded at the same timestamp are counted separately.
A hit timestamped exactly `windowMs` milliseconds before the count time is included, while a hit older by any positive amount is excluded and pruned.
A zero-duration window counts hits at the current timestamp and excludes and prunes earlier hits.
After a short-window count prunes an old hit, a later larger-window count does not recover that hit.

With controllable `Date.now()` values that are not chronological, count includes only retained timestamps in `[now - windowMs, now]`, prunes all retained timestamps below that interval regardless of storage position, and does not count future-dated retained timestamps.
The package declares no runtime or development dependencies, and `npm test` passes using the existing `node --test` script.
Time-dependent tests restore any replaced global time source and other modified process state during cleanup.
out_of_scope: Validation or prescribed error behavior for invalid `windowMs` arguments.
ES module exports, named-export wrapper objects, or additional public Counter methods.
Concurrency, multi-process coordination, persistence, distributed counting, or performance guarantees.

output.notes: Implemented the dependency-free CommonJS Counter with inclusive sliding-window counting, individual timestamp evaluation, irreversible pruning, duplicate support, and deterministic built-in Node.js tests.

Adversarial coverage includes direct class export and arities, exact time capture, duplicate timestamps, inclusive boundaries, irreversible pruning, zero windows, future timestamps, backward clock movement, unordered storage, and dependency metadata.

patterns: When a sliding-window counter encounters future-dated retained hits, prune only timestamps below the lower boundary; retain future hits without counting them so they can become countable when the clock advances.
Use a finite scripted clock that throws on unexpected Date.now calls to verify each operation samples time the required number of times, and restore the global clock in test cleanup.
